problem: Two-stage VLN-CE pipelines use waypoint predictors (ResNet-50, naive RGB-D fusion, heatmap loss only) that ignore obstacles and spatial cues, and zero-shot LLM navigators (e.g. Open-Nav) see images only as text captions, lack history reasoning and cannot backtrack.
motivation: Real-world deployment suffers from data scarcity and poor generalization, so training-free MLLM navigators are attractive. Their errors compound without a way to recover, and poor waypoints (into obstacles) make this worse, so both the waypoint quality and the navigator's history/backtracking need improvement.
key_idea: Combine an occupancy-aware waypoint predictor (DINOv2 encoder, masked cross-attention RGB-D fusion, depth-derived occupancy BCE loss) with a GPT-4o navigator that uses a history-aware single-expert prompt, multi-step planning and an explicit backtrack action.
insight: Both parts contribute and are complementary: the enhanced predictor alone raises SR 24->26 and lowers NE 7.61->7.11 in the navigator ablation, backtracking alone raises SR to 28 and cuts collisions 0.067->0.044, and together they reach SR 29 / SPL 22.46 / collisions 0.033. In the predictor ablation, the occupancy loss gives the largest %Open jump (82.15->87.26), while DINOv2 and cross-attention give smaller alignment gains. In the real-world test, backtracking raises SR 24->36.
method: DINOv2 encoder: replaces the ImageNet ResNet-50 RGB encoder with DINOv2-Small (similar size); depth encoder unchanged.
Masked cross-attention fusion: replaces the non-linear RGB-D fusion layer; RGB features are queries and depth features are keys/values, with a mask restricting attention to adjacent views.
Occupancy-aware loss: computes minimum horizontal distance per 3-degree bin from depth, builds a 120x12 occupancy mask, and adds BCE(P, M) to the MSE heatmap loss, L = L_vis + 0.5*L_occ.

History-aware single-expert prompt: one GPT-4o call per step gets instruction, history, candidate waypoint images and action options, and outputs one action; extends MapGPT's single-expert design to VLN-CE.
Multi-scale turning and RAM tags: adds slight (~30 deg) and sharp (~90 deg) turn options and RAM object labels for candidate views and history entries.

Adaptive path planning with backtrack: the model writes a multi-step plan/thought each step that is fed back in, and has an extra action 'Move back to last position in an opposite direction' to undo mistakes.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (gpt-4o-2024-08-06, frozen, zero-shot navigator) + DINOv2-Small/ResNet-50 depth waypoint predictor (trained)
setting.training_data: Waypoint predictor trained on MP3D waypoint data following Hong et al. (AdamW, bs128, lr 1e-6, 300 epochs); navigator is training-free
setting.observation: panoramic RGB-D (12 views at 30 deg), RAM object tags
setting.action_space: candidate waypoints with turn descriptions (slight/sharp left/right), plus move-back; executed as low-level continuous actions

numbers.eval_set_note: 100 episodes, following the Open-Nav evaluation protocol
numbers.evidence: Table 1 (Comparison on Simulated Environment in R2R-CE) and Table 4 row #4

numbers.backbone: DINOv2-S + depth ResNet-50 with cross-attention, trained
numbers.evidence: Table 3 (Comparison of the waypoint predictors on MP3D Val-Unseen), row Ours

numbers_note: The R2R-CE results use only a 100-episode subset. The paper's text says 'Ours' has NE 7.01, which is worse than Open-Nav-GPT4 (6.70). Real-world Ours w/o Backtrack: SR 24, NE 3.28.
results: With GPT-4o and the enhanced predictor, the method reaches SR 29 / OSR 51 / SPL 22.46 on 100 R2R-CE val-unseen episodes, beating the best zero-shot baseline Open-Nav-GPT4 (SR 19, SPL 16.10), though it still trails supervised methods (ETPNav SR 52, BEVBert SR 60). On the real robot it reaches SR 36 vs RecBERT's 20, and the new predictor gets the best %Open (87.26).
limitations: Evaluated on only 100 R2R-CE episodes and 25 real-world instructions, and NE (7.01) is not better than Open-Nav-GPT4 (6.70); large gap remains to supervised methods.
Backtracking is one step only (undo to the last position), and it depends on the closed GPT-4o API.
Semantic understanding relies on RAM tags rather than richer scene representations.
builds_on: Hong et al. waypoint predictor (Bridging the gap)
